findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest by default.

findings.issue_category: no bucket ACL / public access controls
findings.description: The bucket has no ACL set and no public access block configuration, leaving it reliant on account defaults and providing no explicit protection against public exposure.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for a bucket storing ledger export data, meaning sensitive financial data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so model artifacts are stored without encryption at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational runbooks (potentially containing sensitive operational details) are stored unencrypted at rest.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid canned S3 ACL; if this is intended to be a custom/typo'd ACL like 'log-delivery-write', it may still grant broad write access to the audit trail bucket, undermining integrity of audit logs. At minimum this is a misconfiguration that should be reviewed for unintended access grants.

The object is uploaded without specifying server-side encryption (kms_key_id or server_side_encryption), and is placed into a bucket (reports_archive) that itself lacks default encryption, resulting in cleartext storage of the uploaded file.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be deleted without versioning protection, increasing risk of irreversible data loss if misused, though this is more of an operational concern it also removes a safeguard against accidental/malicious destruction of stored data.
